A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same G-NoCL/DISCOBER research. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original continual-learning experiments on PACS, DomainNet, CCT and CIFAR-10-W, together with component ablations, scaling analyses and prompt comparisons.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds ensemble-selection comparisons and quantitative and qualitative analyses of generated-image diversity.

M1.justification: The two-stage prompt refinement, 50 prompts, four generators, RMD-based probabilistic ensembling and online prototype updates remain unchanged. Applying the existing ensemble procedure to web data does not document a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Both versions use PACS, DomainNet, CCT and CIFAR-10-W with the same classification coverage. The added diversity analyses use existing PACS and CIFAR-10 categories, and web and generated data were already represented. Newly discussed blurry or noisy learning scenarios are not newly evaluated.

E2.justification: v2 Table 7 adds equal-weight, k-highest/k-lowest RMD and inverse-probability comparators within the retained ER, MIR, ASER and LiDER settings, extending v1's DER-only selection-rule comparison. Table 8 adds these comparisons on web data with ER and ASER. The principal CL baseline roster remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Primary splits, backbones, training budgets and accuracy metrics remain unchanged. Added analyses specify 220 generated images per class, LPIPS/DISTS and Rarity Score measurements, and a web-data pool five times the manually annotated size with 80% CLIP filtering. Appendix J additionally states 10% oversampling, conflicting with the retained 20% main-text description; the actual collection fraction is unclear.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands validation through ensemble-rule comparisons across additional learners, web-data selection experiments, RMD/Rarity Score examples, and direct prompt- and ensemble-diversity analyses using LPIPS, DISTS and Rarity Score. These additions in Section 4.6 and Appendices E, F and L supplement the retained component, scaling and prompt analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions state that experiments use five random seeds and report averages with standard errors. No changed run-count policy, confidence-interval procedure or significance-testing practice is documented.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1 and 3–5 and the matched older appendix result tables retain their numerical values. New Tables 7–8 and Figures 6 and 14–16 add substantial comparison and diversity results. For example, Table 8 reports web-PACS ER OOD AAUC of 32.02 for k-highest RMD versus 29.07 for DISCOBER. These are additional results under the new protocol, not improvements over v1's main scores.

T1.justification: The RMD definition, generator-selection probabilities and incremental mean/covariance updates in Equations 1–5 are unchanged. v2 adds explanatory discussion and empirical metrics, but no new theorem, proof, formal assumption or mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain category-name-only generative continual learning, prompt diversification and complexity-guided ensembling, with the same broad ID/OOD performance claims. The abstract's increased emphasis on G-NoCL and stronger wording do not establish a different scientific scope.

C2.justification: v2 explains choosing RMD because it does not require real samples, attributes the web-data OOD reversal to domain overlap, and explains why retaining representative samples can reduce Rarity Score relative to equal-weight ensembling. It also discusses the limited style sensitivity of LPIPS/DISTS. The concluding limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a generated-dataset access link in the abstract and explicitly clarifies that testing uses categories seen so far. Additional sample-count and web-filtering details are supplied, although the conflicting 10% and 20% collection descriptions limit reproducibility. Dataset accessibility was not externally verified.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially revises CL positioning toward realistic stream setups and the data-acquisition gap, replacing detailed method-family and generative-replay discussion. v2 also introduces substantial literature on image-generation evaluation, including Rarity Score, TopP&R, LPIPS and DISTS, while removing numerous references from the shortened web-data and replay discussions.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites clarify the abstract, introduction, prompt-refiner and evaluation descriptions. The standalone generated-versus-web-data section is removed, with selected material folded into Appendix C, and sections are reorganized. Much of the method, existing results discussion and extensive prompt catalog retains its wording.

P2.justification: v2 adds two tables and five figures, redraws the framework and prompt-refiner diagrams, and relocates several retained displays. Page margins are substantially reduced throughout. Matching the retained plots and illustrations establishes that their relocation and renumbering do not constitute new experimental evidence.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the existing sampling and diversity rationale better supported through comparisons beyond DER and direct image-diversity measurements. The web-data failure case and generated-dataset link also improve assessability. The gain is limited by new reporting problems, including conflicting 10%/20% web-collection descriptions and claims of consistent superiority that Table 7 does not fully support.
